questions.question: What is a computer program?
questions.correctAnswer: A set of instructions a computer follows
questions.explanation: A program is a list of steps written in code; the computer reads the code and carries out each step in order.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Programs are instructions.

questions.question: What is hardware?
questions.correctAnswer: The physical parts of a computer
questions.explanation: Hardware includes the keyboard, screen, and processor.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hardware is the physical parts.

questions.question: What is software?
questions.correctAnswer: The programs and apps that run on a computer
distractors: The physical parts of a computer
questions.explanation: Software is the code that tells hardware what to do.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Software is the programs.

questions.question: What does CPU stand for?
questions.correctAnswer: Central Processing Unit
questions.explanation: The CPU is the brain of the computer.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The CPU is the brain.

questions.question: What does RAM do?
questions.correctAnswer: It holds data the computer is using right now
questions.explanation: RAM only holds data while the computer is on, so it is fast but small; when you open an app, its data is loaded into RAM.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: RAM is short-term memory.

questions.question: What is the difference between RAM and storage?
questions.correctAnswer: RAM is temporary memory; storage keeps files long-term
questions.explanation: RAM clears when the computer turns off; storage keeps files.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: RAM is temporary, storage is long-term.

questions.question: What is an operating system?
questions.correctAnswer: Software that manages the computer and lets you use it
questions.explanation: Examples include Windows, macOS, and ChromeOS.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The OS manages the computer.

questions.question: What is a file?
questions.correctAnswer: A collection of data stored with a name
questions.explanation: Files hold documents, photos, and programs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Files store data.

questions.question: What is a folder?
questions.correctAnswer: A container that organizes files
questions.explanation: Folders are named boxes on a drive, and folders can hold other folders, so you can build a tree like School > Math > Homework.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Folders organize files.

questions.question: What does .pdf stand for?
questions.correctAnswer: Portable Document Format
questions.explanation: PDFs keep the same layout on any device, which is why teachers send worksheets and forms as PDFs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: PDF is Portable Document Format.

questions.question: What is a .jpg file?
questions.correctAnswer: A common image file format
questions.explanation: JPG squeezes photo data into a small file, so photos load fast online, but saving a JPG again and again slowly lowers its quality.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: JPG is for images.

questions.question: What is the internet?
questions.correctAnswer: A global network connecting computers
questions.explanation: The internet is made of millions of connected computers and cables under the sea; no single company owns it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The internet links computers.

questions.question: What is a web browser?
questions.correctAnswer: Software used to view websites
questions.explanation: Browsers like Chrome and Safari show web pages.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Browsers show web pages.

questions.question: What is a search engine?
questions.correctAnswer: A tool that finds web pages for your search words
questions.explanation: Search engines like Google index the web.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Search engines find pages.

questions.question: What is a URL?
questions.correctAnswer: The address of a web page
questions.explanation: A URL has parts: the protocol (https://), the domain (like google.com), and the path to the exact page.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A URL is a web address.

questions.question: What does HTTP stand for?
questions.correctAnswer: HyperText Transfer Protocol
questions.explanation: HTTP is the protocol browsers use to load pages.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: HTTP loads web pages.

questions.question: What does HTTPS add to HTTP?
questions.correctAnswer: Encryption for a secure connection
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses encryption, so anyone spying on the network sees scrambled data instead of your passwords; look for the padlock icon.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: HTTPS means secure.

questions.question: What is a strong password?
questions.correctAnswer: A long mix of letters, numbers, and symbols that you do not share
questions.explanation: A long password is hard to guess because every extra character multiplies the combinations; a password manager can create and store one for you.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Strong passwords are long and private.

questions.question: What is two-factor authentication?
questions.correctAnswer: A second check, like a code, after your password
questions.explanation: Two-factor adds a code from your phone or app.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two-factor adds a second check.

questions.question: What is phishing?
questions.correctAnswer: A fake message that tries to trick you into sharing information
questions.explanation: Phishing emails and texts pretend to be trusted sources.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Phishing tries to trick you.

questions.question: What should you do with a suspicious email asking for your password?
questions.correctAnswer: Do not click or reply; report it
questions.explanation: Real companies never ask for passwords by email.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Do not click suspicious links.

questions.question: What is malware?
questions.correctAnswer: Harmful software made to damage or steal from a computer
questions.explanation: Malware includes viruses, spyware, and ransomware.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Malware is harmful software.

questions.question: What is a computer virus?
questions.correctAnswer: Malware that copies itself and harms a computer
questions.explanation: Viruses spread and can damage files or steal data.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Viruses copy and harm.

questions.question: What is ransomware?
questions.correctAnswer: Malware that locks files and demands payment
questions.explanation: Ransomware encrypts files until a ransom is paid.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ransomware locks your files.

questions.question: What is a firewall?
questions.correctAnswer: Software or hardware that blocks unwanted network access
questions.explanation: A firewall checks every message coming in or out and drops the ones that break its rules, like a guard at a gate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Firewalls block intruders.

questions.question: What is a VPN?
questions.correctAnswer: A service that encrypts your internet connection
questions.explanation: A VPN hides your traffic from others on the network.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A VPN encrypts your connection.

questions.question: What is personal information?
questions.correctAnswer: Details that identify you, like your name, address, or phone number
questions.explanation: Personal information should stay private online.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Keep personal info private.

questions.question: What is a digital footprint?
questions.correctAnswer: The trail of data you leave online
questions.explanation: Everything you post and share adds to your footprint.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Your footprint follows you.

questions.question: What is cyberbullying?
questions.correctAnswer: Bullying that happens online or through messages
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying uses phones, social media, or games to hurt someone.
questions.memoryHook: Cyberbullying happens online.

questions.question: What should you do if someone bullies you online?
questions.correctAnswer: Save evidence, block them, and tell a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Adults can help stop cyberbullying.
questions.memoryHook: Save, block, tell an adult.

questions.question: What is copyright?
questions.correctAnswer: The legal right of a creator to control their work
questions.explanation: Copyright protects books, music, photos, and videos.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Copyright protects creators.

questions.question: What does it mean to cite a source?
questions.correctAnswer: To give credit to where information came from
questions.explanation: A citation lists the author, title, and date, so a reader can find the same source and check your facts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cite to give credit.

questions.question: What is plagiarism?
questions.correctAnswer: Using someone else's work without giving credit
questions.explanation: Copying a paragraph and changing a few words is still plagiarism; only your own words and ideas, or a proper quote with credit, are safe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plagiarism is copying without credit.

questions.question: What is a reliable source?
questions.correctAnswer: A source with evidence, expertise, and no clear bias
questions.explanation: Check who wrote it, when it was written, and whether other trusted sources agree; a page with no author or date is a warning sign.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Reliable sources show evidence.

questions.question: What is fake news?
questions.correctAnswer: False information presented as real news
distractors: A news story you disagree with
A news story with an opinion
A news story from another country
questions.explanation: Fake news often uses shocking headlines and made-up quotes to get clicks; check the story on a known news site before you believe it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fake news misleads.

questions.question: How can you check if online information is true?
questions.correctAnswer: Compare several reliable sources and check the author and date
distractors: Trust it because it looks nice
questions.explanation: Checking multiple sources helps you spot false claims.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Check several sources.

questions.question: What is an algorithm?
questions.correctAnswer: A step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem
questions.explanation: Algorithms are clear steps, like a recipe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Algorithms are step-by-step.

questions.question: What is a variable in coding?
questions.correctAnswer: A named place that stores a value
questions.explanation: Variables hold data that can change, like score = 0.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Variables store values.

questions.question: What is a loop in coding?
questions.correctAnswer: Code that repeats until a condition is met
questions.explanation: Loops repeat actions, like counting to ten.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Loops repeat code.

questions.question: What is a conditional in coding?
questions.correctAnswer: Code that runs only if a condition is true
questions.explanation: Conditionals use if and else to make choices.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: If and else make choices.

questions.question: What is a function in coding?
questions.correctAnswer: A reusable block of code that does a task
questions.explanation: A function has a name and takes inputs; calling it by name runs the same steps again, so one fix repairs every place that uses it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Functions reuse code.

questions.question: What is a bug in coding?
questions.correctAnswer: An error in a program
questions.explanation: A bug can be a typo, a wrong number, or a step in the wrong order; even one wrong character can stop a whole program.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bugs are errors.

questions.question: What is debugging?
questions.correctAnswer: Finding and fixing errors in a program
distractors: Writing code for the first time
questions.explanation: Debuggers test small pieces, print values to see what the program really does, and fix one error at a time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Debugging fixes errors.

questions.question: What is binary?
questions.correctAnswer: A number system using only 0 and 1
questions.explanation: Computers store data as binary digits, or bits.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Binary is 0 and 1.

questions.question: What is a bit?
questions.correctAnswer: The smallest unit of data, a 0 or a 1
questions.explanation: Eight bits make one byte, and every letter, number, and color on screen is stored as a pattern of bits.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A bit is 0 or 1.

questions.question: How many bits are in a byte?
questions.explanation: Eight bits make one byte, and a byte can store one character, like the letter A.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A byte is 8 bits.

questions.question: What is a pixel?
questions.correctAnswer: The smallest dot of color on a screen
questions.explanation: Images are made of many pixels.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pixels make up images.

questions.question: What is cloud storage?
questions.correctAnswer: Storing files on the internet instead of on your device
questions.explanation: Your files live on a company's servers, so you can open them from any device, but you need internet and the company's account to reach them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cloud storage is online.

questions.question: What is a backup?
questions.correctAnswer: A copy of your files kept in case the original is lost
questions.explanation: Keep a second copy somewhere else, like a USB drive or the cloud, so one broken device cannot take your work with it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Backups save your work.

questions.question: Why should you back up your files?
questions.correctAnswer: So you can recover them if your device breaks or files are lost
questions.explanation: Devices break, files get deleted by mistake, and viruses can lock files; a backup is the only way to get them back.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Backups protect your files.

questions.question: What is email?
questions.correctAnswer: Messages sent over the internet
questions.explanation: Email travels from your provider's server to the other person's server, which is why it arrives even when their computer is off.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Email sends messages.

questions.question: What is spam?
questions.correctAnswer: Unwanted bulk messages, often ads or scams
questions.explanation: Spam clogs inboxes and can carry scams.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Spam is unwanted bulk mail.

questions.question: What is a social media account?
questions.correctAnswer: An online profile you use to share and connect
questions.explanation: An account has a username, a password, and privacy settings; what you post under it can be seen by anyone you allow to follow you.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Social media connects people.

questions.question: What is a good rule for posting online?
questions.correctAnswer: Do not post anything you would not want everyone to see
questions.explanation: Once posted, content can spread and stay online.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Think before you post.

questions.question: What is netiquette?
questions.correctAnswer: Good manners for communicating online
questions.explanation: Netiquette also means not typing in ALL CAPS, which reads as shouting, and not sharing other people's photos without asking.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Netiquette is online manners.

questions.question: What is a spreadsheet?
questions.correctAnswer: A program that organizes data in rows and columns
questions.explanation: Spreadsheets like Google Sheets calculate and sort data.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Spreadsheets organize data.

questions.question: What is a word processor?
questions.correctAnswer: A program for writing and editing documents
questions.explanation: Word processors like Google Docs help you write.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Word processors help you write.

questions.question: What is a presentation program?
questions.correctAnswer: A program for making slides to show ideas
questions.explanation: Presentation programs like Google Slides make slide decks.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Presentations make slides.

questions.question: What is data?
questions.correctAnswer: Facts and numbers collected and stored
questions.explanation: Data can be numbers, words, images, or sounds.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Data is collected facts.

questions.question: What is a database?
questions.correctAnswer: An organized collection of data
questions.explanation: Databases store and sort large amounts of data.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Databases organize data.

questions.question: What is artificial intelligence (AI)?
questions.correctAnswer: Computer systems that learn and make decisions from data
questions.explanation: AI does not understand like a person; it finds patterns in huge amounts of examples and guesses the most likely answer.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: AI learns from data.

questions.question: What is machine learning?
questions.correctAnswer: AI that improves by learning from data
distractors: A machine that thinks like a human
questions.explanation: Machine learning trains models on examples.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Machine learning learns from examples.

questions.question: What is a chatbot?
questions.correctAnswer: A program that talks with people using text
questions.explanation: A chatbot matches your words to answers it was trained on; it can sound sure even when it is wrong, so check important answers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Chatbots talk with people.

questions.question: Why should you check AI answers?
questions.correctAnswer: AI can make mistakes or give false information
questions.explanation: Always verify AI output with reliable sources.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Check AI answers.

questions.question: What is a QR code?
questions.correctAnswer: A square barcode that links to a website or information
questions.explanation: A QR code stores a link in black and white squares; your phone camera reads the pattern and opens the link.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: QR codes link to information.

questions.question: What is Wi-Fi?
questions.correctAnswer: Wireless technology that connects devices to a network
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi uses radio waves, so walls and distance weaken the signal; that is why the connection is faster near the router.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wi-Fi connects wirelessly.

questions.question: What is a router?
questions.correctAnswer: A device that connects your network to the internet
questions.explanation: Routers send data between your home network and the internet.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Routers connect you to the internet.

questions.question: What is the difference between the internet and the web?
questions.correctAnswer: The internet is the network; the web is pages on that network
distractors: The internet is a web page
questions.explanation: The internet also carries email, games, and video calls; the web is only the pages you open in a browser.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The web runs on the internet.

questions.question: What is a download?
questions.correctAnswer: Copying a file from the internet to your device
distractors: Sending a file to the internet
questions.explanation: A download copies the file, so the original stays on the server and you get your own copy on your device.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Downloads bring files to you.

questions.question: What is an upload?
questions.correctAnswer: Sending a file from your device to the internet
distractors: Copying a file to your device
questions.explanation: An upload sends your copy to a server, which is how photos reach social media and homework reaches your teacher.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Uploads send files out.

questions.question: What is a cookie on a website?
questions.correctAnswer: A small file a site stores to remember you
questions.explanation: Cookies remember logins and preferences.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cookies remember you.

questions.question: What is a pop-up?
questions.correctAnswer: A small window that opens on top of a web page
questions.explanation: Pop-ups can be ads or alerts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pop-ups open on top.

questions.question: What should you do before downloading a file?
questions.correctAnswer: Make sure it comes from a trusted source
questions.explanation: Trusted sources lower the risk of malware.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Download only from trusted sources.

questions.question: What is antivirus software?
questions.correctAnswer: Software that finds and removes malware
questions.explanation: Antivirus compares files to a list of known malware and watches for suspicious behavior, then quarantines anything it catches.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Antivirus blocks malware.

questions.question: What is a digital citizen?
questions.correctAnswer: Someone who uses technology responsibly and respectfully
questions.explanation: Digital citizens follow rules, respect others, and stay safe online.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Digital citizens act responsibly.

questions.question: What is the best way to share a file with a classmate?
questions.correctAnswer: Use a school-approved sharing tool or link
questions.explanation: School tools keep sharing safe and controlled.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Use school-approved sharing.

questions.question: What is a keyboard shortcut?
questions.correctAnswer: Keys pressed together to do a task quickly
questions.explanation: Shortcuts like Ctrl+C copy text fast.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Shortcuts save time.

questions.question: What does Ctrl+C do?
questions.correctAnswer: Copies selected text or files
questions.explanation: Ctrl+C copies to the clipboard, a hidden holding spot; the original text stays where it was.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ctrl+C copies.

questions.question: What does Ctrl+V do?
questions.correctAnswer: Pastes copied text or files
questions.explanation: Ctrl+V drops the clipboard copy at the cursor; you can paste the same copy many times until you copy something else.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ctrl+V pastes.

questions.question: What does Ctrl+Z do?
questions.correctAnswer: Undoes the last action
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Z steps back through your last changes one at a time; pressing it again undoes the change before that.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ctrl+Z undoes.

questions.question: What does Ctrl+S do?
questions.correctAnswer: Saves the current file
questions.explanation: Ctrl+S writes your work to the file on disk; without saving, a crash loses everything since the last save.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ctrl+S saves.

questions.question: What is the difference between save and save as?
questions.correctAnswer: Save updates the current file; Save As creates a new copy
questions.explanation: Save As lets you pick a new name or location.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Save As makes a new copy.

questions.question: What is a screenshot?
questions.correctAnswer: A picture of what is on your screen
questions.explanation: A screenshot saves exactly what is on screen as an image file, which is handy for showing an error to a teacher.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Screenshots capture the screen.

questions.question: What is a hyperlink?
questions.correctAnswer: Text or an image that links to another page
questions.explanation: Clicking a hyperlink jumps to another page.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hyperlinks jump to pages.

questions.question: What is a domain name?
questions.correctAnswer: The readable address of a website, like example.com
questions.explanation: A domain name is rented, not owned forever; the owner pays each year to keep using it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Domains are readable addresses.

questions.question: What is an IP address?
questions.correctAnswer: A number that identifies a device on a network
questions.explanation: IP addresses are like phone numbers for devices.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: IP addresses identify devices.

questions.question: What is a server?
questions.correctAnswer: A computer that provides data or services to other computers
questions.explanation: Servers host websites and store data.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Servers provide services.

questions.question: What is a client?
questions.correctAnswer: A device or program that requests data from a server
questions.explanation: Your browser is a client that asks servers for pages.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Clients request data.

questions.question: What is open source software?
questions.correctAnswer: Software whose code is free to view and change
questions.explanation: Open source code is public, so anyone can read it, report bugs, or suggest fixes; Linux and Firefox are open source.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Open source is free to view.

questions.question: What is a programmer?
questions.correctAnswer: A person who writes code
distractors: A person who fixes hardware only
A person who uses apps only
questions.explanation: Programmers also test, fix bugs, and read other people's code; writing the first draft is only part of the job.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Programmers write code.

questions.question: What is a flowchart?
questions.correctAnswer: A diagram showing the steps of a process
questions.explanation: A flowchart uses shapes: ovals for start and end, rectangles for steps, and diamonds for yes-or-no decisions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Flowcharts map steps.

questions.question: What is pseudocode?
questions.correctAnswer: Plain-language steps describing a program
questions.explanation: Pseudocode uses plain words like 'if the score is over 10, show You win', so you can plan the logic before writing real code.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pseudocode plans in plain words.

questions.question: What is a boolean value?
questions.correctAnswer: True or false
questions.explanation: Booleans come from true-or-false questions, like 'is the player alive?'; they control if-statements and loops.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Booleans are true or false.

questions.question: What is a string in coding?
questions.correctAnswer: Text data, like 'hello'
questions.explanation: Strings hold text in quotes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Strings hold text.

questions.question: What is an integer in coding?
questions.correctAnswer: A whole number, like 7
questions.explanation: Integers cannot hold fractions, so 7 divided by 2 in integer math gives 3, not 3.5.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Integers are whole numbers.

questions.question: What is a list in coding?
questions.correctAnswer: An ordered collection of items
questions.explanation: A list keeps items in order and numbers them from 0, so the first item is at position 0, not 1.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lists store many items.

questions.question: What is the first step in solving a coding problem?
questions.correctAnswer: Understand the problem and plan the steps
questions.explanation: Planning first saves time and errors.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plan before you code.

questions.question: What is a search engine result page?
questions.correctAnswer: The page showing links that match your search
questions.explanation: A results page ranks links by relevance; the top results are often ads, marked as sponsored.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Results list matching pages.

questions.question: How can you make a web search better?
questions.correctAnswer: Use specific keywords and quotes for exact phrases
questions.explanation: Quotes force the exact phrase, and a minus sign drops a word, like cats -musical to skip the show.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Specific keywords find better results.

questions.question: What is a browser tab?
questions.correctAnswer: A page open inside a browser window
questions.explanation: Tabs let you open several pages at once.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tabs hold open pages.
